_doc: Cardinality-cliff DECOMPOSITION on true NVMe, killing a newly-found confound: stream data files live at <data-dir>/streams/ = the BASE /data volume, which on the raw-block multilane cluster is a plain emptyDir on the PD BOOT DISK — so every prior multilane run had the WAL commit path on NVMe but the checkpoint's O(N)-file writeback on a network PD. Here every arm appends '--data-dir /data/wal/0' (last --data-dir wins in main.rs arg parsing) so streams/ AND wal/ all sit on NVMe lane 0 (one fs; shard count is concurrency only, not lanes). Arms decompose the wal-vs-memory gap: memory (no wal, no fsync ever) | nofsync (full wal machinery, --unsafe-disable-fsync: no fsync at all) | ckpt-off (wal + commit fdatasync, checkpoint deferred 1h = off within a bench window) | ref-3s (normal syncfs @3s = PR #4697 config, re-measured on real NVMe). Verdicts: nofsync ~= memory => wal machinery is free, gap is all fsync. ckpt-off ~= nofsync => commit fdatasync is cheap (group-committed), gap is all checkpoint. ref-3s @100k >> the ~10-18k measured with streams-on-PD => the 'residual cliff' in PR #4697 was substantially the boot-disk artifact. Image :ckptoff is built from the perf/wal-lazy-checkpoint worktree (has --wal-checkpoint-interval-ms, --unsafe-disable-fsync, syncfs). Run with IMG_SERVER=europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/vaxine/ds-bench/durable-streams:ckptoff MULTILANE=1 SERVER_LOCAL_SSD_BLOCK=1 SPOT_SERVER=1.
